what: THE EDGE FROM A SCHOLARLY WORK TO THE ENTITIES ITS TITLE NAMES. §VI `relationships/scholarly_discussion/`, which §III.7 asks for and which the coverage table records as MISSING: arda_scholarship held 4,870 rows and no entity edge among them.
what_an_edge_claims: THE WORK'S OWN TITLE NAMES THIS ENTITY. Nothing more. It is not a claim that the paper is ABOUT the entity and it is not a summary of an argument nobody here has read: arda_scholarship is METADATA ONLY -- no article text and no PDF is republished -- so the title is the whole of the evidence available, and every row says so in its own `basis` field.
why_conf_is_EXT_on_every_row: the title is the publisher's own description of its own publication, carried from an OAI-PMH harvest. The archive asserts nothing about Arda on any row here. No row carries a tier, for the reason arda_scholarship gives: the tiers rank claims about Arda, and a bibliographic record is not one.
why_the_yield_is_low_and_why_that_is_the: most of the 2,166 landing-page records are Mythic Circle, a creative-writing magazine, so their titles are poems and stories with no Tolkien name in them. The population is printed beside every count (C224): a low rate over a stated denominator is a measurement; the same rate with the denominator omitted would be an insinuation.

the_match.vocabulary: map/ardaentity.py, built from the collections that DEFINE entity ids, read off `git -C site ls-files` and never a glob.
the_match.comparison: whole words through ardatext.words_of -- the archive's ONE matcher. A raw lower() would fail on the mixed NFC/NFD these datasets carry.
the_match.matched_by: `full name` or `one word of a person's name`, published on every edge so a reader can tell an edge made on `Aragorn II Elessar` from one made on `Aragorn`.
the_match.containment: where one matched name is inside another, only the longer stands. `Bilbo Baggins` does not also emit `Bilbo` and `Baggins`.
the_match.ambiguity: a name borne by more than one record is published with every candidate and no winner. The owner's ruling of 5 August.

title_stoplist_why: names that are ALSO ordinary titles of poems and stories. Every entry was found by running the match with this list EMPTY and reading what it caught: Dale is a town of Men and Jo Anna Dale's surname; Bill is Sam's pony and Pecos Bill; Ruby, Lily and Rose are hobbit given names and the titles of three Mythic Circle poems. IT BELONGS TO THIS FILE AND NOT TO THE SHARED VOCABULARY, because the same names are perfectly safe in an artifact's tenure prose.

searched_and_empty.what_it_means: the row's title was matched, as whole words, against every one of the 1694 names in the vocabulary and none of them stands in it. THE TITLE NAMES NO ENTITY THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS -- which is a fact about the title and about the archive's registers, and says nothing at all about what the article discusses. The archive does not hold the article.
